evidence: Ehsani et al., MSR'26, arXiv 2601.15195. 24,014/33,596 merged (71.48%). Table 1 CI coef -0.1579, OR 85%. 'each additional failed CI check decreases the odds of a merge by about 15%.' CI from 'status of the last commit in the PR'.
correction: The paper never says how open PRs are treated; 71.48% = merged/all 33,596 PRs, so open PRs fall into the not-merged group only by implication. Say 'merged/all' and do not call it a stated method.

evidence: Li, Zhang, Hassan, arXiv 2507.15003v1. Finding #2 (Sec. 4.1) text: 'Codex ... 64%, followed by Devin at 49% and GitHub Copilot at 35%'. Table 5 %Accepted gives Human 76.8, Codex 65.3, Devin 48.9, Copilot 38.2, Cursor 51.4, Claude Code 52.5.
correction: Full title adds ': How Autonomous Coding Agents Are Reshaping Software Engineering'. The 64/49/35 figures come from Sec. 4.1 Finding #2, not Sec. 4.2 Table 5, and Table 5 gives 65.3/48.9/38.2 (human 76.8). Cite one source consistently. The quote about cutting review time 10x is Finding #5 and does not support the acceptance claim.

evidence: Watanabe, Li, Kashiwa, Reid, Iida, Hassan; accepted at TOSEM. Table 2: 475/567 agentic merged (83.77%) vs 516/567 human (91.00%). Sec. 4.3: 54.94% (261) of merged Agentic-PRs merged as a single commit, i.e. without revision.
correction: Say '54.94% of MERGED Claude Code PRs were merged without revision (single commit)'. The base is merged PRs, not all PRs. 'Closed' here means PRs with a final decision.

evidence: Strauss & Schulze (Anhalt UAS), MSR 2026, Zenodo paper.pdf. Sec. 3.2: 'we remove PRs with status open'. Sec. 4.1: 'regular acceptance rate is 79.89%'. Sec. 4.2: '84.1% of the Agentic PRs are closed by then' (60 min) vs 56.5% human.
correction: Location: 79.89% is in Sec. 4.1 (open-PR removal is in Sec. 3.2), and 84.1% within 60 min is in Sec. 4.2. Full title adds ': An Exploratory Study'.

evidence: Branco, Canelas, Gamboa, Fonseca, MSR'26 (doi 10.1145/3793302.3793621). Sec. 2: 'We define Auto-Merge as merging a PR without reviews or review comments'; 'mochilang/mochi and MontrealAI/AGI-Alpha-Agent-v0 represent 37.2% of PRs'.
correction: The paper calls its data 'AIDev' (~33,000 PRs from popular repos, >=100 stars), which is effectively AIDev-pop. 'Many merge with no review' is qualitative: auto-merge is bimodal per repo (Sec. 3.1) and agentic PRs are auto-merged more often than human ones. No single overall auto-merge share was found.

evidence: Nachuma & Zibran, MSR'26, arXiv 2602.19441. Sec. 3.3: 33,596 PRs, 71.5% merged, 21.6% closed, 6.9% open. Abstract/Sec. 4.3.1: 'reviewer engagement has the strongest correlation with successful integration'. Sec. 4.3.4: 'Neither iteration intensity nor test additions are significantly associated with merge outcomes'.
correction: Full title: 'When AI Teammates Meet Code Review: Collaboration Signals Shaping the Integration of Agent-Authored Pull Requests'. The outcome split is in Sec. 3.3, not Sec. 2. Tests: Sec. 4.3.4.

evidence: Dao Sy Duy Minh et al., arXiv 2601.00753. Abstract: 'agents excel at narrow automation (28.3% of PRs merge instantly)' over 33,707 PRs. Table 2 (Sec. 2.1) Instant %: Codex 42.9, Copilot 0.1.
correction: Location for per-agent numbers: Table 2, Sec. 2.1. 'Instant' is labeled '<1m' in the Fig. 3 caption with no formal definition, and the table does not state its denominator. Arxiv preprint, no venue.

evidence: Actual title: 'Do Autonomous Agents Contribute Test Code? A Study of Tests in Agentic Pull Requests' (Haque, Ingale, Csallner), arXiv 2601.03556. Table 4 (closed PRs): Devin non-test 60.6 vs test 44.1; 'Merge rates are largely similar across PRs and agents.'
correction: Use the full title above. No MSR 2026 venue is shown on arXiv (no comments or journal-ref) [verify venue]. Claim supported: Claude 72.1 vs 70.6, Codex 85.2 vs 86.2, Copilot 56.8 vs 53.8, Cursor 71.6 vs 75.6, Devin 44.1 vs 60.6.
